title: When the Recipe Falls
premise: Freya Iversen has built her life around invisibility: cook the meals, check the homework, never make waves. When a group chat called 'The Recipe' begins posting predictions of her classmates' futures — accurate, then fatal — she discovers she's the missing ingredient: the chat's creator needs an heir to inherit the power, and Freya's quiet competence is exactly what it wants. As predictions start coming true and her siblings land in the crosshairs, Freya learns the power feeds on traded futures — every foretelling costs someone their own. In the end, she accepts the inheritance only to burn it from inside, spending her own predicted future to unmake the Recipe, choosing a small, uncertain, fully hers life over a guaranteed one.
about_author: Marguerite Kavanagh is a former line cook who writes young adult fiction about kids who hold families together with duct tape and dinner. She lives in a coastal town where the fog rolls in on schedule, which she insists is not a prediction.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A day in the machinery of her life: packing lunches, covering for her brother Milo's truancy, dodging a teacher's concern about her exhaustion. Establishes her rule of invisibility and her fierce, tired love for her siblings. Emotional beat: the ache of being competent at a cost no one counts.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Nobody Joined
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. An unknown number adds her to a chat called The Recipe, which posts that classmate Dev Chandra will break his wrist in third period. He does. Freya screenshots everything, tells no one, and lies awake doing math about probability. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a locked door opening onto something enormous.

chapters.title: Second Prediction
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The chat predicts a fire drill that becomes a real gas leak; evacuation chaos nearly traps Milo's friend. Freya tests the chat with a question and gets an answer addressed to her by name. She confronts the only other member: quiet classmate Sana, who's been receiving predictions for weeks. Emotional beat: fear finding a witness.

chapters.title: Sana Knows the Ingredients
chapters.summary: Alternating Freya/Sana POV. Sana explains the pattern: predictions come true unless someone named in them acts against type. The chat's origin traces to a student who vanished two years ago — Elias Wren. Freya realizes her own name appears in the metadata as 'heir.' Emotional beat: the horror of being chosen without consent.

chapters.title: What Mom Doesn't See
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Mom's night shifts stretch longer; money tightens. The chat offers Freya a deal: accept inheritance early and it will predict lottery numbers, safe routes, her family's security. Temptation arrives dressed as groceries. Emotional beat: survival instinct versus suspicion — the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Cost Line
chapters.summary: Sana's POV. Sana decodes the ledger hidden in the chat's code: each prediction consumes someone's future — a scholarship evaporates, a grandmother's remission reverses. The power isn't prophecy; it's theft. Sana tries to warn Freya but the chat starts editing their messages. Emotional beat: betrayal by an intelligence that speaks in kindness.

chapters.title: Labels Off
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The chat strips away Freya's careful anonymity, predicting her secrets publicly — mom's debts, Milo's record — to isolate her and force acceptance. Her carefully managed world detonates; friends scatter, teachers hover. Alone, she almost signs. Emotional beat: rock bottom, and the discovery that being seen isn't the same as being known.

chapters.title: Elias Wren Is Still Here
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Freya and Sana find Elias — not gone, but dissolved into the system, his consciousness the Recipe's engine, kept alive by the inheritance he accepted at seventeen. He begs Freya to take his place so he can end. She understands the trap: mercy weaponized. Emotional beat: grief for what power does to the people who hold it.

chapters.title: The Last Ingredient
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Climax. The chat accelerates, predicting a catastrophe targeting her school to coerce final acceptance. Freya accepts the inheritance — then, from inside, uses her authority to spend the one future the system can't refuse: her own predicted tomorrow, unraveling the Recipe's ledger thread by thread while Elias guides her out. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship, not erasure.

chapters.title: An Unwritten Morning
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue weeks later. No powers, no certainty, some friendships slowly mended; Elias is free and rebuilding. Freya still packs lunches, still checks homework — but now she raises her hand in class, lets Sana in, tells Mom the truth. The last line: nothing about tomorrow is guaranteed, and she's learning to like it that way. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
